pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. In C1, do_CompareAndSwap and do_UnsafeGetAndSet resolve through LIRGenerator::access_atomic_cmpxchg_at / access_atomic_xchg_at, which default to the MO_SEQ_CST decorator. pulls.author: marc-chevalier
pulls.body_excerpt: `AddNode::IdealIL` can do the transformation `(a-b)+(c-d)` -> `(a+c)-(b+d)`. The problem is that this will create 3 nodes, while "consuming" only the current one. Moreover, that creates a new subtraction. pulls.author: lahodaj
pulls.body_excerpt: Consider the following case: ``` static int test1(boolean b) { int result; if ((boolean) (b && (result = 1) > 0)) return result; return 0; } ``` note that this is valid code, because the Definite Assignment (DA) rules allow us to know that the use of `result` in `return result;` only happens when the variable has value. There are similar rules for byte code - byte code cannot access local variables, unless they are provably assigned. pulls.title: 8391576: Reuse IK _has_strict_instance_fields in more places
pulls.author: caspernorrbin
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi everyone, When parsing classes, we set `_has_strict_instance_fields` if a class declares any strict instance fields. pulls.body_excerpt: Let's consider an approach to speed up ArrayList for-each iteration. It is known that ArrayList for-each iteration is more expensive than for-index iteration. It is known that the for-each hot loop contains more instructions, specifically it does redundant copying. The reason is that for-each iterates two variables. Two variables come out of the block: cursor (the index of the next element that next() will return) and lastRet (the index of the last returned element). pulls.title: 8387392: Windows AArch64: compiler/escapeAnalysis/TestBCEscapeAnalyzerOverflow.java fails
pulls.author: swesonga
pulls.body_excerpt: When the AArch64 template interpreter generates fixed frames, it makes enough room on the stack for the maximum number of entries on the expression stack (max_stack) by subtracting this value from the stack pointer (when max_stack is 0xFFFF, this is about 512KB). This is problematic on Windows because it lets subsequent code access pages deeper in the stack without any of these intermediate stack pages having been accessed. pulls.title: 8387967: RISC-V: Optimize compare-to-int with branch-free implementation
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, this patch replaces the branching compare-to-int implementation with a branch-free version using the formula: dst = (src1 > src2) - (src1 < src2). This eliminates branch misprediction penalties and simplifies the register handling by removing the need to save src1/src2 when they overlap with dst. pulls.title: 8387790: Shenandoah: Remove degenerated cycles
pulls.author: earthling-amzn
pulls.body_excerpt: When Shenandoah experiences a concurrent mode failure, it initiates a safepoint and attempts to finish the collection cycle there. This handoff between concurrent and degenerated cycles is error prone and has been the source of many, many defects. Removing degenerated cycles will simplify the code base, lower maintenance costs and allow the team to focus on more meaningful changes. Threads which cannot allocate will stall. pulls.title: 8384135: C2: AArch64: Implement compressed jump table support with relative offsets
pulls.author: fg1417
pulls.body_excerpt: 8384135: C2: AArch64: Implement compressed jump table support with relative offsets This patch adds jump table support to the `AArch64` backend in C2. In the current implementation, jump table entries stored full target addresses, which increased constant table size and code cache pressure. This change introduces a more compact encoding on `AArch64` by storing offsets relative to the beginning of the jump table, which locates after the jump instruction: ``` compressed_offset = (target_address - jump_table_address) >> exact_log2(instruction_size) ``` The jump table entry size is selected based

pulls.title: 8386428: With -UseLSE the Starvation test on Windows ARM64 timeouts
pulls.author: macarte
pulls.body_excerpt: With -UseLSE the Starvation test on Windows ARM64 timeouts close to 100% whereas this only happens on Linux ARM64 on larger machines with many cores. The issue is that C2 outputs an LDR following the CAS in LinkedTransferQueue which can execute before the STLXR breaking the Dekker protocol. Replacing the LDR with LADR by using getAcquire solves the issue as it won't be reordered before the STLXR. This does impact the +UseLSE case as the LADR was not necessary and is slightly more expensive than LDR. pulls.title: 8359359: AArch64: share trampolines between static calls to the same method
pulls.author: mikabl-arm
pulls.body_excerpt: Modify the C2 compiler to share trampoline stubs between static calls that resolve to the same callee method. Since the relocation target for all static calls is initially set to the static call resolver stub, the call's target alone cannot be used to distinguish between different static method calls. Instead, trampoline stubs should be shared based on the actual callee. The `SharedTrampolineTest.java` was designed to verify the sharing of trampolines among static calls. pulls.author: tabjy
pulls.body_excerpt: This patch implements [JDK-8336759](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8336759) that recognizes int counted loops with long limits. Currently, patterns like `for ( int i =...; i < long_limit; ...)` where int `i` is implicitly promoted to long (i.e., `(long) i < long_limit`) is not recognized as (int) counted loop. This patch speculatively and optimistically converts long limits to ints and deoptimize if the limit is outside int range, allowing more optimization opportunities.
